chunks: "An accelerometer measures acceleration along an axis, more precisely specific force. Inside a MEMS accelerometer there is a tiny proof mass held by springs.
When the package accelerates, the mass lags behind and shifts a little, and that changes the capacitance between the mass and fixed electrodes, which a circuit turns into a number.
A nice consequence is that at rest on a table it reads 1 g upward on the vertical axis, because the table is pushing the case up, and in free fall it reads zero.
That is why it can find which way is down. A gyroscope measures angular velocity, how fast something is rotating about an axis, in degrees per second.
A MEMS gyro keeps a small mass vibrating.

When you rotate the chip, the Coriolis force pushes the mass sideways in a direction perpendicular to its vibration, and that small sideways motion, again sensed capacitively, is proportional to the rotation rate.
So the accelerometer tells me which way gravity points and how I am being pushed, the gyro tells me how fast I am turning.
If I want an angle from the gyro I have to integrate its output, and that is where drift comes from, which is why the two are usually combined."
